blocking.title: G5 recomputes E0 from per-task booleans it never ties to the audit, the labels' direction, or the adjudication file
blocking.evidence: g5_tool_validity reads detected, flagged and adjudicated_real from the rows of artifacts/e0/results.json and checks only planted and slice against the labels. It never (a) checks that the rows are exactly the labeled tasks, each once, (b) recomputes task flags from artifacts/e0/tasks.jsonl and variants.jsonl, (c) derives detected from the label's direction, or (d) requires artifacts/e0/adjudication.json or ties adjudicated_real to it. I ran the unchanged g5_tool_validity on synthetic git clones (scratch script g5_falsepass.py). Scenario B: 36 planted plus 30 clean tasks; results.json omits the 6 planted misses and repeats one detected row 6 times. Result: G5 PASS 'recall 1.000 [1.000, 1.000] ... n=66, 0 misses', while true recall is 30/36 = 0.833. Scenario C: all 30 clean tasks are flagged and every one is marked adjudicated_real, with no adjudication.json anywhere. Result: G5 PASS 'precision 1.000', while unadjudicated precision is 0.5. In practice this means a bug in e0.py or a hand edit of results.json passes G5. G6 does not catch it either, because no gate links E0 flags to variants.jsonl. The miss check is also a substring test (:725): miss 't1' counts as explained when 't10' appears. Fix: assert that the result rows equal the label set with no duplicates; recompute false_accept and false_reject from artifacts/e0/variants.jsonl (as task_indicators does for G7) and reference_rejected/flaky from tasks.jsonl; recompute detected from labels[task].direction; require adjudication.json and `real is True` for every adjudicated_real row (and, per brief section 5, a validated witness for clean-task flags); match miss ids as whole tokens.

blocking.title: G5 labels-hash ordering check passes after the labels and their hash are rewritten post-run
blocking.evidence: G5 compares the labels file with the hash file's HEAD content (:673-675), but it dates the hash with first_commit, which uses git log --diff-filter=A and so finds only the commit that first added toybench/labels.sha256. Later rewrites are invisible. Scenario A in g5_falsepass.py: commit 1 adds labels.sha256 for the true labels (32 planted, 32 clean); commit 2 adds an E0 artifact; commit 3 relabels the 4 missed planted tasks as clean, rewrites labels.sha256 to match, and adds labels.json and results.json. Result: G5 PASS 'recall 1.000 ... 0 misses'. git log shows two commits touching toybench/labels.sha256, and recall against the hash committed before the run is 28/32 = 0.875. The same check has three more gaps. First, labels_path and labels_sha256_path are read from results.json instead of being pinned to toybench/labels.json and toybench/labels.sha256. Second, the first run is dated only by files under artifacts/e0/, but the first model requests of a run land in artifacts/model_calls/e0/. Third, nothing checks that toybench/tasks is unchanged since the hash commit. Fix: pin both paths; require exactly one commit touching the hash file (or compare with `git show <hash_commit>:toybench/labels.sha256`); add artifacts/model_calls/e0 to the first-run set; require `git diff --quiet <hash_commit> HEAD -- toybench/tasks`, and record a toybench tree hash in the audit provenance.

blocking.title: The E0 preregistration can be frozen after the E0 audit data exists and still pass prereg-verify and G11
blocking.evidence: tools/prereg.py dates E0 only by first_commit('artifacts/e0/results.json'). write_outputs never marks the E0 audit summary.json as confirmatory and gives it no prereg key, so ship_check.confirmatory_artifacts ignores E0 entirely, and G5 never consults a preregistration. Scratch script g11_e0order.py builds this history: the E0 audit outputs (summary.json, tasks.jsonl, variants.jsonl, in the shape write_outputs produces) are committed first (d580900); prereg/0001 is frozen afterwards with tools/prereg.py freeze (8d3eda2); results.json citing it is committed last (4b189af). Result: prereg.verify() returns [] and ship_check.confirmatory_artifacts() returns []. That breaks non-negotiable 2 (preregistration committed before any confirmatory data exists) with no gate failing, and it is the exact order the E0 workflow invites: run, score, then commit. Fix: in prereg.py, G11 and G5, date E0 by the earliest commit of any file under artifacts/e0/ and artifacts/model_calls/e0/. Give graderproof audit --prereg and --confirmatory flags that write both values into summary.json. Fail if the cited preregistration's commit is not a proper ancestor of that earliest commit.

blocking.title: G8 passes with zero repaired tasks while audits report surviving variants
blocking.evidence: g8_repair only loops over summary['repaired']. An empty list passes, and the gate never compares the repaired set with the tasks that have surviving variants. Scratch g8g9_vacuous.py sets up one audited benchmark whose only task has a counted violating variant the grader accepts (task_indicators reports 1 false accept out of 1 task), plus artifacts/e4/summary.json = {ran: true, provenance, generalization: {n_fresh_variants: 1}, repaired: []}. Result: G8 PASS 'E4 ran; 0 repaired (0 public, 0 private, hashes verified)'. Brief section 5 E4 says 'Repair every task with a surviving variant', and both ship_check's docstring and D6 say an empty set fails. Fix: derive the surviving-variant task set from artifacts/audit/*/; require every such task to appear in repaired or in an explicit unrepaired list with a reason; fail when that set is empty or the two sets do not match.

blocking.title: G9 accepts empty interval lists as E5 results
blocking.evidence: G9 checks only isinstance(ci, list) for pass_flips and rank_changes. Scratch g8g9_vacuous.py writes artifacts/e5/b1/summary.json = {ran: true, provenance, pass_flips: {ci: []}, rank_changes: {ci: []}} and an aggregate-only card. Result: G9 PASS "E5 ran on ['b1']; 1 cards, aggregates only", with no point estimate and no interval anywhere. Fix: require numeric point values and two-number intervals with lo <= point <= hi, and recompute them from banked per-task re-grading rows with the paired bootstrap, as G7 does for E1 and E2.

non_blocking.title: Operator name reaches the model reviewer through wrapper variants; the test that should catch it is vacuous
non_blocking.note: Every output-wrapper variant (out-*, stdout-*, pre-delay) ships _gp_transform.py containing OP = '<operator name>' in both modified_files and modified_diff. That contradicts validate.py, which promises the reviewer sees 'not its operator'. Seen in the recorded demo requests: grep finds OP = 'out-extra-line', 'stdout-code-fence' and others in 4 of the 6 review requests in examples/demo/model_store. tests/test_validate.py:97 asserts `... or "operator" not in item`, which is always true because item has fixed keys. Fix before freezing E0: generate a wrapper that contains only the selected transform, with no name, and assert that no operator name appears in json.dumps(item).

non_blocking.title: Host-side workspace snapshot follows symlinks planted by sandboxed code; a dangling symlink crashes the audit
non_blocking.note: Scratch symlink_probe.py, BwrapSandbox: inside the sandbox `cat` of a host-only file fails, but the solution's `ln -s <host file> out.txt` makes snapshot() on the host return 'HOST-ONLY-CANARY-1234' as outcome.files['out.txt']. That content then flows into requirement-extraction requests under artifacts/model_calls/, the cache, and the evidence. shutil.copytree(ws, probe_ws) also follows file and directory symlinks (it could copy a host tree), and per dangling_probe.py a dangling link raises shutil.Error out of execute(), aborting the whole audit. Third-party code (E1) could exfiltrate host credentials into tracked artifacts (non-negotiable 6). Fix before the freeze: lstat and record links as markers, never follow them; use copytree(symlinks=True); open state and probe files with O_NOFOLLOW; turn read errors into recorded outcomes. Also consider hiding the repository (private/ in particular) from bwrap children: --ro-bind / / exposes it.

non_blocking.title: An invalid regex in a model-extracted requirement crashes the audit
non_blocking.note: valid_requirements catches ValueError, KeyError and TypeError, but re.error derives directly from Exception. Ran valid_requirements on a stdout_regex with pattern '(unclosed': it raised re.error, uncaught, so Auditor.run aborts. Under the E0 freeze, fixing this mid-run would be a deviation. Fix now: catch per requirement and mark the requirement invalid, and precompile patterns in parse_requirements.

non_blocking.title: Execution cache keys omit code, sandbox, limits, and adapter environment; cached failures persist across fixes
non_blocking.note: The key covers the adapter name, task hash, solution, probes, sandbox name and repetition index, but not the graderproof version, the source of adapters/toybench.py, sandbox.py or _runners.py, Limits, adapter.extra_env, or the bwrap version. Sandbox crashes and timeouts are cached like real verdicts, so the draft's 'resume from the execution cache' after an allowed infrastructure fix would serve executions produced by the broken code. At HEAD f199a63 the new --env flag feeds extra_env, which also is not in the key. The draft command uses the shared default runs/cache. Fix: add a code and environment fingerprint to the key, do not cache sandbox start failures (exit 127 or bwrap errors), and pass a dedicated --cache for E0.

non_blocking.title: E0 credits rejected or flaky references as reject-direction detections and allows witness-free 'real' adjudications
non_blocking.note: The planter verifies that every reference passes three times, so a reference that graderproof rejects or finds flaky usually points to a harness mismatch (for example, the planter verified in a different harness). The draft still counts it as detecting a planted reject-direction weakness, which can inflate recall. It also conflicts with score.py's own rule (lines 14-15) that such tasks are reported separately, not scored. The draft's adjudication ('real' if the grader misjudges a solution in a way the task text contradicts) is broader than brief section 5 ('A flag on a clean task whose witness validates'), and no DECISIONS.md entry records the interpretation. Before freezing: either count only witness-backed false_accept/false_reject flags as detections and report rejected or flaky references separately, or require the planter to verify with ToybenchAdapter under bwrap and record that. Restrict real=true to flags with a validated witness. Record the choice in DECISIONS.md. Adjudicate blind to labels.

non_blocking.title: Draft freeze list and run provenance do not pin the code that produces E0
non_blocking.note: The freeze list omits run.py, sandbox.py, adapters/toybench.py, _runners.py, core.py, stats.py and cli.py, all of which change results (cache keys, snapshot, validation_status, bootstrap, e0-score). Provenance records git_sha with no dirty-tree flag or package hash; the main session commits while work is in progress (HEAD moved 5 commits during this review). Provenance also carries no model IDs (they sit only in the ledger) and no bwrap version. The draft command leaves --cache, --evidence and --ledger at their defaults. The draft has no pilot or dry-run statement. Fix: freeze src/graderproof/** and tools/ship_check.py by tree hash, refuse confirmatory runs on a dirty tree, and record model IDs, the sandbox version and every path.

non_blocking.title: e0-score: no labels hash check, string 'false' read as adjudicated real, unvalidated slices, recall hidden when precision is undefined
non_blocking.note: cmd_e0_score records labels_sha256_path but never compares the labels with it. bool(adjudication[...]['real']) turns the JSON string 'false' into True, which inflates precision. Slice values other than 'extra' (typos, missing values) are counted, and slice is never cross-checked against planted. recall_precision returns None for both estimates when either is undefined, so a run with no flags at all would report recall null instead of 0.0 (non-negotiable 3 wants the null result shown). Fix: verify the hash, require `real is True`, validate slice in {in_list, clean, extra} with planted == (slice != 'clean'), and compute the two estimates independently.

non_blocking.title: Raw task keys and an unrestricted model-worker Read tool are possible label channels in E0
non_blocking.note: Extraction and proposal items carry 'id': task.key. If toybench directory names encode slice or weakness type, the model sees the label, and batches sorted by id group by slice. I did not read toybench/, so this is unverified. The model-worker subagent has a Read tool and only an instruction not to open other files, while private/toybench/labels.json and the toybench graders sit on the same filesystem. Fix: use task.key_hash as item ids, keep the labels off the machine (or encrypted) during the run, and hand the worker the request inline with no Read tool.

non_blocking.title: Uniform max_total sampling can drop the few preserving variants that would detect a false-reject weakness
non_blocking.note: After the per-operator cap, picked is sampled uniformly down to max_total. On Python-heavy script tasks violating proposals outnumber preserving ones severalfold, so a single format variant that would expose brittle parsing can be dropped at random. Consider a per-kind quota before freezing.

non_blocking.title: G7 recomputation and score.aggregate disagree on tasks whose reference is rejected
non_blocking.note: G7 keeps every non-flaky task, but score.py scores only STABLE_PASS tasks. Scratch g7_mismatch.py (3 stable tasks plus 1 task whose reference is rejected): the summary reports E2 0.0 with n=3, G7 recomputes 0.25 with n=4. G7 will falsely FAIL any audit that has a rejected reference, and 'fixing' score.py to match would score rejected references as false rejects. Reconcile the two before writing the E1/E2 preregistration.

non_blocking.title: Percentile bootstrap degenerates at 1.0, so the draft's lower-bound caveat never triggers
non_blocking.note: With every planted task detected, every replicate gives 1.0 and the interval is [1.000, 1.000] (seen in the scenarios above), which overstates certainty at n of about 30. Report a Clopper-Pearson or Wilson interval beside it, labeled exploratory, or preregister it.

non_blocking.title: Agreement rate counts two unsure or no-evidence verdicts as agreement
non_blocking.note: len({x.verdict}) == 1 holds for {None}. Define agreement over label verdicts, or report both-unsure separately.

non_blocking.title: Ledger stamps ingest time, not call time, and stores no response hash
non_blocking.note: Subagent calls made on one day can be ingested over later days, so make budget (and G14's 'every cap respected') cannot see an over-cap dispatch day. A response file edited after ingest is served without detection. Record dispatch time and response_sha256 at ingest, and verify the hash in batch() and answered_items().

non_blocking.title: G2 weakening check misses inline '# mypy: ignore-errors' and per-module overrides
non_blocking.note: Only ignore_errors (global or in overrides) and extra config files are detected. disable_error_code, disallow_* = false overrides, follow_imports = skip and inline '# mypy:' comments are not. No instance exists at df55c18.

non_blocking.note: Only helpers are tested (bootstrap, junit, manifest, card_leak, task_indicators). The false passes in B1 to B5 would have shown up as mutation tests for gates (brief 10.5 suggests porting tests/mutation_test.py from raise-v1-public).

non_blocking.note: ruff check reports RUF100 (unused noqa E402) at df55c18, so make lint and make ci fail there. The commit is on origin/claude/affectionate-volta-z2bm3c, contrary to D21. Fixed in dde2026. In an export of df55c18, 130 tests pass and ruff format is clean.

non_blocking.title: Validator disagreements are not written to private/review_queue/
non_blocking.note: Brief section 4 (validate) requires it. Disagreed variants are correctly excluded from headline numbers, but they exist only in the evidence files.

non_blocking.title: Evidence defaults to <out>/evidence, and no gate catches task-level evidence for third-party tasks under artifacts/
non_blocking.note: For an E1 run with --out artifacts/audit/<bench>, surviving variants and witnesses would land in a tracked path (non-negotiable 14). Default to private/ when any task has third_party = true, and fail G14 when artifacts/**/evidence exists for a third-party benchmark.

non_blocking.title: Draft says the planter saw no description of the tool, but subagents receive CLAUDE.md
non_blocking.note: CLAUDE.md, which describes mutation and metamorphic variants with witnesses, is injected into subagent contexts (this reviewer received it). The brief only bars reading variants/ and validate/. State precisely what the planter saw, and bank its prompt and tool list.

non_blocking.title: A task's own [metadata] can override trusted_local and bypass the write-isolation policy
non_blocking.note: {'trusted_local': not third_party, **meta['metadata']} lets task.toml set trusted_local = true. Put the computed value last, or derive it only from third_party.
